title: Segmented heartbeat + admission windows to stop short-flow starvation during mixed-length waves
creator: Maya Chen
description: Customer AtlasPay reported repeated incidents where small short-lived inference requests (user typing completions) experienced severe P99 spikes and frequent timeouts during mixed-length traffic waves. Impact was observed across Hosted and Dedicated clusters and replicated in a Private staging deployment. Investigation showed intermittent starvation of short requests caused by a decaying admission reservoir and single-expiry prefetch lifecycle combined with maintenance-induced timer drift. This ticket tracked investigation, a multi-phase hotfix, rollout, and follow-up hardening to prevent recurrence.
root_cause: The admission reservoir used a single shared expiry timestamp to represent in-flight reservation capacity. Under mixed-length waves and during host maintenance windows (NTP/timer drift + private upgrade pauses) the reservoir's expiry values drifted prematurely, causing admission to treat available slots as expired and then over-reserve for long-context requests. That led to head-of-line long-context batches starving short flows. Additionally, the prefetch path did not honor per-length aging and could requeue evicted KV state, amplifying stall duration.
investigation_notes: 2026-01-16: Pager alerted — AtlasPay reported P99 for short requests rose from ~40ms to 420ms, error rate 2.1% on hosted clusters in us-west-2.
2026-01-16: Triaged with infra/oncall. Initial hypothesis: continuous-batcher admission edgecase during maintenance window.
2026-01-18: Reproduced in dedicated-local using synthetic mixed-length traffic generator (60% short, 40% long). Observed admission expiry timestamp collapse after scheduled host restart.
2026-01-20: Correlated spike windows with prefetch eviction churn and KV handoff logs — eviction hysteresis was insufficient for mixed workloads.
2026-01-22: Proof-of-concept implemented: per-length segmented admission windows + heartbeat renewal to extend short-flow reservations while long batches drain.
2026-01-25: Canary rollout to hosted control plane (5% of traffic) — short-request latency improved immediately, no regression on throughput.
2026-02-03: Extended rollout to Dedicated (reserved clusters) with feature flag off for Private by default pending compatibility test.
2026-02-20: Private staging validation completed; flag enabled in private with upgrade window guard.
2026-03-01: Full rollout completed; dashboards show P99 short-request drop to baseline across all hosting modes.
fix_summary: Introduce length-segmented admission windows and a lightweight heartbeat renewal for short-flow reservations, plus an eviction hush timer for prefetch to avoid KV thrash. Changes include: 1) admission reservoir now tracks three length buckets (short/medium/long) with independent expiry and quotas; 2) a periodic heartbeat extends short bucket leases when there is active short-flow pressure; 3) prefetch eviction gains a 200ms hush window after handoff to prevent immediate re-eviction; 4) feature flagging for gradual rollout and an opt-out path for Private upgrade windows.
implementation_steps: Add per-length bucket metadata to admission reservoir (atomic counters + expiry_ts per bucket).
Implement heartbeat renewal task bounded to 1ms overhead per host when short-traffic pressure > 10qps.
Introduce prefetch hush window (configurable, default 200ms) to avoid eviction thrash under KV churn.
Add feature flag admission.segmented_mode with default off for private until validated.
Add telemetry: per-bucket inflight counts, bucket expiry drift, prefetch-hush hits, and short-request P99 slicing.
Unit + integration tests for mixed-length replay harness; load tests in dedicated staging at 1.5x peak load.
Document config knobs and rollback path in runbook.
Coordinate with SRE for canary rollout and alerts tuning.
Ship runtime-1.22 containing the changes and update console release notes.
Post-deploy validation for 72h followed by full enablement.
Backfill telemetry and expose per-customer shortflow SLA view in Console.
Create follow-up ENG tasks to evaluate longer-term admission strategies.
rollout_plan: Canary: hosted API 5% traffic for 24h with tight SLO guardrails (P50/P95/P99 for short requests).
If canary stable, expand hosted to 25% for 48h and run synthetic mixed-length generator.
Dedicated: apply to low-risk reserved clusters (non-critical customers) after hosted 25% success.
Private: keep feature flag off by default; enable per-customer after manual upgrade window and smoke test.
Full enablement after 72h stable canary and green synthetic tests.
monitoring_playbook: Create alert: shortflow.P99 > baseline + 150ms for 5m triggers P0 oncall.
Synthetic job: mixed-length 60/40 replay every 15m — compare short P99 pre/post feature enablement.
Runbook steps to temporarily lower long-batch concurrency or toggle admission.segmented_mode=false as fast rollback.
SLO regression policy: automated rollback if shortflow error rate >1.5% for 10m during rollout.
Notify AtlasPay CS and their engineering contact on deploy windows and post-deploy metrics.
rollback_plan: Flip admission.segmented_mode feature flag off (global) — fast path rollback.
If feature-flag flip not sufficient, revert runtime-1.22 deployment on host pools with elevated risk.
Coordinate with SRE to temporarily limit long-batch window (max tokens) to restore shortflow capacity.
Notify customers and open post-rollback incident review if rollback triggered.
